mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 5% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when unemployment is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP and consumer spending indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when both GDP and consumer spending grow.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in federal funds rate above 2% may signal tightening monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when federal funds rate exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative when industrial production increases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in CPI suggests inflationary pressures, which may negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when CPI increases by 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment and high payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when unemployment is low and payroll employment is high.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when housing starts increase by 5%.
